assessment.support_scope: This research was funded by EuroQol Research Foundation (EQ project 2014210).
assessment.reason: The study primarily examines caregiver HRQOL, caregiver burden, and their determinants. It also directly evaluates the ability of EQ-5D-5L to discriminate HRQOL across caregiver-burden groups. EuroQol Research Foundation funded this research.

items.statement: Caregiver HRQOL had a statistically significant inverse correlation with caregiver burden, but the effect size was small.

values.direction: Higher burden was associated with lower HRQOL.

source: Full article, §3.1 The EQ-5D Capacity to Discriminate HRQOL between Caregivers’ Burden Groups, paragraph 1

items.statement: Mean EQ-5D index values differed across caregiver-burden groups. The absence-of-claudication group differed from both higher-burden groups, but the two higher-burden groups did not differ significantly.

values.direction: no detected difference in mean EQ-5D index

source: Full article, §3.1 The EQ-5D Capacity to Discriminate HRQOL between Caregivers’ Burden Groups

items.statement: More than 20% of caregivers reported moderate, severe, or extreme problems in the EQ-5D pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression dimensions.

items.statement: The authors conclude that EQ-5D-5L is sensitive to differences in HRQOL between caregivers with different levels of caregiver burden.
source: Full article, Abstract, final sentence
Full article, §4 Discussion, paragraph 2

items.statement: The authors state that EQ-5D can capture caregiver HRQOL effects and can support the inclusion of caregiver effects in economic evaluations.
source: Full article, §4 Discussion, paragraphs 5–6

items.statement: The BURQOL-RD database was collected for other objectives, and the high level of missing caregiver-age data prevented analysis of caregiver age in relation to HRQOL.
source: Full article, §4 Limitations, paragraph 1

items.statement: Children in France received EQ-5D-5L instead of EQ-5D-Y, which may have influenced the HRQOL ratings.
source: Full article, §4 Limitations, paragraph 1

items.statement: The child utility values came from a US valuation study that used a method different from usual EQ-5D-3L TTO studies, so the child values were on a different scale. The authors state that this did not affect the analysis because the values were used only as explanatory variables.
source: Full article, §4 Limitations, paragraph 1

items.label: Caregiver HRQOL spillover effects
items.description: Health effects of rare diseases that occur in informal caregivers and may be included with patient effects in economic evaluation.
source: Full article, §4 Discussion, paragraphs 2 and 6
